observations: Five-letter toy sum hash starts FEBCD at twenty against ABCDE pattern sum fifteen.
First slide subtracts outgoing F six and adds incoming A one, yielding EBCDA sum fifteen; diagram marks four kept letters.
Checking that candidate rejects E versus A, demonstrating collision. Next-flag batch reaches true ABCDE, then direct check confirms all five letters.
Eight slides use five initial values plus sixteen boundary values, twenty-one versus forty-five full-window reads; reveal distinguishes constant-cost updates from required collision verification.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Separate updating a hash from verifying a match.

whyCool: A window can reuse almost all its work, while a cheap summary still needs a careful final check.
caveat: Simple order-insensitive sum is deliberately collision-prone; work counters cover sum updates, not all verification operations.
effort: Prediction, manual slide, false flag check, batched advance, true match check, screenshot and reveal.
